prompt:
Read the following email from an international student and write a reply.

Dear Li Ming,
I’ve got a class assignment to make an oral report on an ancient Chinese scientist, but I’m not sure how to prepare for it. Can you give me some advice? Thank you for your help.
Yours,
Paul

Write your answer in about 100 words on the ANSWER SHEET.
Do not use your own name in your email; use “Li Ming” instead. (10 points)
body: I’m glad to offer some advice on your oral report. First, choose a scientist whose story interests you, such as Zhang Heng, who invented the world’s first seismograph. Next, collect reliable information from library books and museum websites, focusing on his major achievements and their influence. Then, organize your report around one or two vivid stories rather than a long list of facts, and use pictures or models to make it more engaging. Finally, rehearse several times so that you can speak fluently and confidently.
I hope these tips help. Good luck with your report!

prompt:
Write an essay based on the picture and the chart below. In your essay, you should
1) describe the picture and the chart briefly,
2) interpret the implied meaning, and
3) give your comments.
Write your answer in 160-200 words on the ANSWER SHEET. (20 points)

【图画】一处标着“市民健身区”的小公园里，人们在散步、跑步、锻炼；一个男孩说：“家门口新建的小公园真不错！”
【图表】某市近三年公园数量（单位：座）：2020 年 406，2021 年 532，2022 年 670
body: The picture and the chart reflect a pleasant change in urban life. In the picture, residents are walking, jogging and exercising happily in a public fitness area, and a boy exclaims, “The new little park near my home is wonderful!” The chart shows that the number of parks in a city rose steadily from 406 in 2020 to 532 in 2021, and then to 670 in 2022, an increase of about 65% in just two years.

The implied meaning is clear: more and more small parks are being built right on people’s doorsteps, greatly improving the quality of their daily lives. This trend results from both the government’s commitment to people-centered urban planning and citizens’ growing awareness of health. These “pocket parks” offer convenient places for exercise, relaxation and social contact, making cities greener and more livable.

In my view, this practice deserves wider promotion. Planners should make full use of idle land to create more green spaces, while residents should take good care of these facilities. After all, a city truly becomes a home when everyone can enjoy nature just a few steps away.

prompt:
Suppose you and Jack are going to do a survey on the protection of old houses in an ancient town. Write him an email to
1) put forward your plan, and
2) ask for his opinion.
Write your answer in about 100 words on the ANSWER SHEET.
Do not use your own name in your email; use “Li Ming” instead. (10 points)
body: I’m writing to share my plan for our survey on the protection of old houses in the ancient town. I suggest we spend the first weekend of next month there. On Saturday, we could photograph the old houses and record their current condition. On Sunday, we could interview local residents and officials to learn what has been done to protect these buildings and what problems remain. After that, we can write a report together with our suggestions.
What do you think of this plan? Please let me know if you have any better ideas.

prompt:
Write an essay based on the chart below. In your writing, you should
1) describe and interpret the chart, and
2) give your comments.
Write your answer in about 150 words on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)

【图表】某高校劳动实践课学生主要收获调查（条形图）：提升了动手能力 84.80%，学习了相关知识 91.30%，提升了合作能力 32.60%，感觉到心情舒畅 54.40%
body: The chart shows what students at a university gained from their labor practice course. Learning relevant knowledge tops the list at 91.3%, closely followed by improving practical skills at 84.8%. Meanwhile, 54.4% of the students reported feeling happier and more relaxed, while only 32.6% believed their teamwork ability had improved.

These figures suggest that the course has achieved remarkable success. By working with their own hands, students not only learn useful knowledge that textbooks cannot offer but also become more capable in real life. Moreover, physical work serves as a good way to relieve the stress of study. However, the low percentage for teamwork indicates that cooperation has not received enough attention.

In my opinion, labor education is an indispensable part of higher education. Universities should continue to offer such courses and design more group tasks, so that students can develop practical skills and a cooperative spirit at the same time.
